title: The optimality of an (s, S) hiring policy on a workforce planning problem with fixed recruitment costs and binomial turnover
summary: We study a finite-horizon nonstationary workforce planning problem in which staff turnover in each period follows a binomial distribution whose parameters depend on the post-hiring workforce level. The model incorporates a fixed hiring cost that is incurred whenever recruitment occurs, regardless of the number of employees hired; this represents explicit (e.g. administration costs) or implicit (e.g. team disruption) factors that are commonplace in workforce planning.
